title: Potage Parmentier (leek and potato soup)

ingredients.name: chicken stock, water, or some combination
parsley, chervril, tarragon, or chive garni

steps.text: Slice white and tender green parts of leeks along long axis. Wash, then chop. Sautee in large saucepan with butter.
Cut potatoes to 3/4 inch cubes. Add to leeks. Add enough water to cover by 1/2 inch.
Bring to boil, partially cover, reduce heat to low, then simmer until tender, about 30-40 minutes.

Process vegetables in several batches in a mouli (best), or through a food processer or blender, or press with a potato masher. Additional water or milk can be added if too thick. The soup can be served directly, or returned to saucepan and reheated when ready to serve. OPTIONAL: To each bowl, add a spoonful of heavy cream, yogurt or a small pat of softened butter. Sprinkle with minced parsley or chopped chives.

attribution.name: Lorraine Spector (possibly originally from Cooks Illustrated)

notes: Variations, or Soupe Du Jour In the beginning, add chopped carrots or tomatoes. OR, half-way through add diced cauliflower, cucumbers, broccoli, zucchini, or lima beans. OR, 5 minutes before the end of cooking add diced, cooked leftover vegetables. OR, can replace part of water with milk, or add powdered milk. OR, make it creamy by adding 1/2 C heavy cream just before serving. Flavoring - add pepper, marjoram, basil, savory and/or bay leaf CHILLED: Add a little more salt and 1/2 C cream before refrigerating, then taste again before serving. OR, add a bunch watercress leaves and stems for last 5 minutes of cooking. Puree.
